style.description:
@inheritdoc

In the case of a tree, the style of its #spans will be `PLAIN` unless they change from its style.

spans.description:
Nested spans within this span. These inherit the style from this node and perhaps add a nested style. These may
be leaf spans or tree to support arbitrary nesting.

title:
A piece of parsed documentation markup with more than one formatting style. These spans are used to contain other
spans when styles nest.

For example, in the case of a link within an emphasized string: `_unless using a {@link Type}._`, you will end up
with four nodes:
- DocumentationSpanTree, style EM, no text
  - DocumentationSpan, style PLAIN, text "unless using a "
  - DocumentationReference (style LINK)
  - DocumentationSpan, style PLAIN, text "."

This means that when rendering spans recursively, one ignores PLAIN style as usual since here it means "same as
parent".

Other examples of how inline spans can nest:
- a paragraph with _regular and **strong** emphasis_
- a _[link](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyperlink) inside an emphasis_
- _`code` and ~~struck-through~~ inside an emphasis_
- [a **strong** link](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/strong)
name: DocumentationSpanTree
